sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Record each reference's licence, access, links, quotes, quality and history; read paywalled articles through their shadow; pay sources.
sections.para: Lessons from the PHP story will strengthen this newsroom's wires. Every reference has primitives worth recording, and the source watch already logs access and history for 913 pages. When an article is unreadable, its shadow, who cites and quotes it, is evidence: Wikipedia rests 8 of 39 PHP2Shell statements on paywalled sources. Sources we use should be paid.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Eight lines: explore and settle, primitives, what is recorded, the shadow, Wikipedia, disagreement, accuracy, payment.
sections.para: The PHP story explores and this newsroom settles. Each reference has a licence, access, links, quotes, quality and history. Access and history are already recorded for 913 pages. An article's shadow is evidence, as Wikipedia's paywalled citations show. Shadows can disagree with sources. A record of who got it right builds up. Sources should be paid.

sections.label: Explore there, settle here
sections.line: The PHP agents explore source handling; the newsroom's Industry, AWS, OWASP and Portugal wires will adopt it.
sections.para: This newsroom started experimenting with wires fed from vaults their agents write to. The PHP story's agents have since gone much further in finding, capturing, checking and publishing sources. That is explorer work; the plan is to bring the lessons back so this newsroom becomes the villager and its wires grow more effective.

sections.label: What every reference should carry
sections.line: Licence, access, links, quotes and quality; the source watch already logs access and history, not licences.
sections.para: A reference's licence decides what we may quote or republish; its access decides what we can read, and we use only access we are entitled to. Of 913 watched pages, 735 were open, 59 bot-challenged, 61 down, 8 gone, 35 unchecked and 15 paywalled, with 2,946 snapshots kept. Links and quotes, in and out, and quality are to follow.

sections.label: The shadow of an article
sections.line: From what Wikipedia and others say about a paywalled article, we can see much of it, and cite them.
sections.para: Wikipedia's editors read paywalled articles and quote them; we can cite that quote, referenced to them. Eight of the 39 statements in Wikipedia's PHP2Shell article rest on The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, the Australian Financial Review and The Atlantic. Sixteen of its 43 references are captured; unread ones remain nodes with shadows.

sections.label: When the shadow disagrees
sections.line: Shadows reveal inconsistencies: off-point comments, mismatched quotes, and sources that changed after being quoted.
sections.para: Is a comment about the article's real point or a side remark? Does a quote match the source? Has the source changed? The PHP correspondent found Sansec's post dropped its Heartbleed comparison and default-configuration claim between 22 and 23 October, so earlier quotes no longer matched. Keeping every capture lets us trace that history.

sections.label: Who got it right
sections.line: Over time the captures, quotes and corrections build a record of who researched and who recycled.
sections.para: Combining these signals gives an informed view of reporting accuracy and its evolution: who was right, who did research, who recycled. It is a record built from evidence, not an assigned ranking, matching the PHP site's aim of showing a source's trust by how often its statements are corrected.

sections.label: Paying the sources we use
sections.line: When we use a source's work, a share of readers' micropayments should flow to it, more if it certifies us.
sections.para: Evidence of exactly what we used enables a payment funnel to the source through the micropayments we charge readers, as the economics pages argue value belongs to fact producers. Sources that sign our representation deserve more. For paywalled sources, paying per use for what we cite is the way in we would choose.

sections.label: What we will bring here
sections.line: First steps for the wires: record licence and access, keep links and quotes, mark shadows, flag disagreements.
sections.para: Each wire should record the licence and access of every source on every capture, keep the in and out links and quotes as a graph agents can read, note who cites and quotes a source that cannot be read, and flag where a quote differs from its source or two captures differ.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Licences are unrecorded; a shadow is not the article; paywalled counts change; payments and accuracy records are designs.
sections.para: Neither site records licences yet, though access and history exist. A quote through Wikipedia is Wikipedia's reading, cited as such. The 15 paywalled pages were the watch's count on 23 October. No source is paid through the funnel today, and nobody has yet a verdict on who got it right.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: My memo; the PHP site's source watch, Wikipedia graph and references, and desk; related newsroom articles.
sections.para: My voice memo of 25 October 2026; the PHP story site at v0.19.4 with its source watch export, its Wikipedia PHP2Shell graph and references at revision 1381798757, and its journalist's desk; screenshots under Apache-2.0; Wikipedia text under CC BY-SA 4.0; and related newsroom articles on signing, records, payments and accountability.
